title: Shared Python Libraries
summary: Package vetted Spark utilities as a versioned Python wheel, test and build it in CI, and deliver it through a Fabric Environment so every notebook and pipeline imports the same code.
audience: Data engineers, platform engineers, technical leads

pages.title: Overview
pages.description: Why copied notebook helpers drift, the wheel-plus-Environment approach, when to use it and a map of the playbook.

pages.title: Designing the library
pages.description: From notebook cells to a library API: the transform, projection and call pattern, full_load_overwrite and incremental merge helpers, and API design rules.

pages.title: Packaging and building a wheel
pages.description: pyproject.toml with the src layout, repo structure, the complete module code, unit tests and building and validating the wheel locally.

pages.title: Installing in a Fabric Environment
pages.description: Upload, publish and attach the wheel, Quick versus Full publish mode, session start impact, why not %pip in pipelines, and using the library in a notebook.

pages.title: CI/CD with GitHub Actions
pages.description: Test, build once and promote the same wheel to DEV, TST and PRD Environments with OIDC sign-in and the Fabric Environment REST API.

pages.title: Options, operations, checklist
pages.description: Distribution options compared (Environment, feed, Lakehouse Files, %run), testing without an Environment, governance, troubleshooting and the validation checklist.
